newsitem.title: USA: VLSI to unveil one-chip set-top decoder.
newsitem.headline: VLSI to unveil one-chip set-top decoder.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc plans to unveil Monday an audio and video decoder in a single chip with a technology it says will make it a leader in emerging set-top box markets for direct broadcast satellite television and other applications.
With the audio/video decoder, VLSI will unveil a suite of chip devices and software that together provide all the parts needed to build digital set-top boxs, officials said.

The San Jose, Calif.-based electronics company said the product is designed for consumer entertainment set-top box markets of direct broadcast satellite receivers, digital video disc players (DVDs) and digital cable set-top boxes.

Paul Vroomen, vice president and general manager of VLSI's consumer digital entertainment group, told Reuters that VLSI sees a huge opportunity beginning with direct satellite broadcast and moving later in the decade with DVD players. Vroomen said the markets for DVD players and cable digital players are new but are expected to burgeon around 1998.
VLSI's new chip is an advanced audio and video decoder chip based on the industry's MPEG2 standard.
Vroomen said what is different with VLSI's chip is that it uses the same processing technology to do both audio and video decoding, rather than two separate processing tasks occurring.

This allows VLSI's product to be considerably cheaper than other set-top box solutions, Vroomen said. Its chip will be sold for $30 based on a 10,000-piece volume pricing. It will be available in October.
Set-top box decoders decompress signals that have been squeezed or compressed for rapid transmission back into the full signals to be viewed or heard on televisions or personal computers.
Set-top boxes also convert digital signals used in fiber optic transmission back into analog signals or broadcast signals to be used on regular televisions.
